lessons.title: Introduction to Python

content.title: What is Python?
content.text: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language known for readable syntax and a large ecosystem of libraries. It is widely used in web development, automation, data analysis, artificial intelligence, scientific computing and scripting.

content.title: Python Syntax
content.text: Python uses indentation to define blocks of code. Unlike languages that use braces, Python relies on consistent indentation.

key_points: Python is a general-purpose programming language.
Python code is designed to be readable.

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types

content.title: Variables
content.text: A variable is a name that refers to a value. Python variables do not require an explicit type declaration.

content.title: Common Data Types
content.text: Common built-in Python types include int for whole numbers, float for decimal numbers, str for text, bool for True or False values, list for ordered collections, tuple for immutable ordered collections, set for unique values and dict for key-value pairs.

key_points: Python variables are created through assignment.
Boolean values are True and False.

lessons.title: Operators and Input

content.title: Arithmetic Operators
content.text: Python supports arithmetic operators such as +, -, *, /, //, %, and **.

content.title: Arithmetic
content.code:
a = 10
b = 3
print(a + b)
print(a // b)
print(a % b)
print(a ** b)

content.title: Comparison and Logical Operators
content.text: Comparison operators such as ==, !=, >, <, >= and <= compare values. Logical operators and, or and not combine or reverse conditions.

content.title: Input
content.code:
name = input("Enter your name: ")
print("Hello", name)

key_points: input() reads user input as a string.

content.title: if Statements
content.text: An if statement executes a block of code when its condition evaluates to True.

content.title: if, elif and else
Nested Conditions
content.text: An if statement can contain another conditional statement. However, deeply nested conditions should be avoided when simpler logic is possible.

lessons.title: Loops

content.title: for Loops
content.text: A for loop iterates over items in an iterable such as a list, string, tuple or range.

content.title: while Loops
content.text: A while loop repeatedly executes its block while a condition remains True.

content.title: break and continue
content.text: break terminates the loop immediately. continue skips the remaining statements in the current iteration and proceeds to the next iteration.

key_points: range() commonly generates sequences of numbers.
while loops continue while their condition is true.
continue skips to the next iteration.

content.title: Lists
content.text: A list is an ordered, mutable collection that can contain multiple values.

content.title: Indexing and Slicing
content.text: Python sequences use zero-based indexing. Slicing can extract a portion of a sequence using start:stop:step.

content.title: Tuples
content.text: A tuple is an ordered collection that cannot be modified after creation.

content.title: Sets
content.text: A set is an unordered collection of unique elements. Sets are useful for membership testing and removing duplicate values.

lessons.title: Dictionaries and Strings

content.title: Dictionaries
content.text: A dictionary stores data as key-value pairs. Keys are used to retrieve associated values.

content.title: Strings
content.text: A string is a sequence of characters. Strings support indexing, slicing and many useful methods.

content.title: Formatted Strings
content.code:
name = "Jayasree"
age = 22
print(f"My name is {name} and I am {age} years old.")

key_points: Dictionary keys are used to access values.
String methods can transform or inspect text.

content.title: What is a Function?
content.text: A function is a reusable block of code designed to perform a particular task. Functions help organize programs and reduce repeated code.

content.title: Defining a Function
content.code:
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

message = greet("Jayasree")
print(message)

content.title: Parameters and Arguments
content.text: A parameter is a variable defined in a function declaration. An argument is the value supplied when calling the function.

content.title: Default Parameter
content.code:
def greet(name="Guest"):
    print("Hello", name)

greet()
greet("Jayasree")

content.title: Return Values
content.text: The return statement sends a value back to the code that called the function.

lessons.title: Exceptions, Modules and Files

content.title: Exceptions
content.text: Exceptions are errors detected during program execution. Python provides try and except blocks for handling expected errors.

content.title: Exception Handling
Modules
content.text: A module is a Python file containing definitions and statements that can be imported and reused in another program.

content.title: Basic File Handling
content.text: Python can open files using the open() function. The with statement is commonly used because it ensures that the file is properly closed.

content.title: Reading a File
content.code:
with open("data.txt", "r") as file:
    content = file.read()
    print(content)

key_points: try and except can handle exceptions.
Modules allow code to be reused.
The with statement is useful for resource management.
